summary: Organizers can mark a guest as VIP from the guest list and narrow the list to VIPs. The flag is stored on the guest; the list shows it inline and the existing group filter gains a VIP option.

checkpoints.title: Store the VIP flag on a guest
checkpoints.intent: The type, the service call and the store action exist before any UI touches them, so the two UI checkpoints build on something already proven.
acceptance: Given a guest, when toggleVip(id) is called, then the store flips is_vip immediately (optimistic) and PATCHes { is_vip } to the guest endpoint
Given the PATCH fails, then the store restores the previous value and surfaces the API's error message

checkpoints.title: Toggle VIP from the guest row
checkpoints.intent: The flag becomes visible and editable where organizers already work — inline in the row, no modal.
acceptance: Given a guest row, when the star is tapped, then it fills and the guest is VIP without a page reload
Given a VIP guest, then the row shows the filled star to screen readers as 'VIP' in the current language

screens: guest list with one VIP guest (desktop)

checkpoints.title: Filter the guest list to VIPs
checkpoints.intent: Adds VIP to the existing group-filter dropdown rather than a new control — the repo's filter idiom.
acceptance: Given the filter dropdown, when 'VIP' is chosen, then only VIP guests are listed and the trigger shows the VIP label
Given the VIP filter is active, when a guest's star is cleared, then that guest leaves the list

screens: filter dropdown open with VIP row
list filtered to VIPs, trigger showing VIP

out_of_scope: Bulk-marking VIPs from the import sheet
risks: Backend: does the guest serializer accept is_vip yet? Probe the live API before cp-01 (401 = exists, 404 = absent).
